title: Rectangle and Sector regions are treated as open curves in Integral and the Cauchy style
repro: ?ns=newfeat with F = 1/(z-2) and one shape, a Rectangle 1.5<Re z<2.5, -0.5<Im z<0.5. Press 7 (Integral). Then select the rectangle in the Shapes list. Also: a sector (c=1, r=1, t1=-60, t2=60) with F=1/(z-1.5). And Phase (2) > Cauchy style with a rectangle selected, F=z^2.
observed: With nothing selected the chip says 'Draw a curve or a bounded region to integrate along it.' even though a bounded rectangle (or sector) exists. With the rectangle selected the chip reads 'Rectangle 1, ∫γ F(z) dz 6.2832i'. That is the open-curve form: there is no (1/2πi)∮, no winding number, no zeros − poles, no Cauchy check at the probe, and no dashed gap. The right plane is also not refit, so the end of the path and its label sit off-screen. In the Cauchy style the pane note says 'select a closed curve or a bounded region' while the rectangle is selected, and it plots plain F everywhere. Disc, polygon, annulus and formula regions all work.
expected: The boundary of a rectangle or a bounded sector is one positively oriented closed curve: ∮ = 2πi·Res, a winding count, a zeros/poles check, and F inside / 0 outside in the Cauchy style.
fix_hint: region.js: K.rect.boundary returns 4 separate seg() pieces and K.sector returns seg+arc+seg, all with closed:false. app.js curvePieces/integralGeom then set closed = comps.every(c => c.closed), and they skip any area with an open piece ('if (!sel && kindType(s)==='area' && pieces.some(c=>!c.closed)) continue'). Fix: in curvePieces, for t==='area', join consecutive boundary pieces whose endpoints meet into one closed polygon before the orientation step, or give rect and sector a single closed poly boundary. Also call fitRight() in Integral mode when the selection changes the set of integrated items.

verdict.evidence:
I reproduced the finding in my own headless Chrome harness (test/verify_features_0_cdp, ?ns=verify_features_0, command file in the scratchpad, v1.js) and confirmed it in the code.

What the app showed (the #calcChip text):
- Rectangle 1.5<Re z<2.5, -0.5<Im z<0.5, F=1/(z-2), Integral mode, nothing selected: "Draw a curve or a bounded region to integrate along it." The bounded rectangle is skipped.
- The same rectangle after selecting its Shapes row: "Rectangle 1 ∫γ F(z) dz 6.2832i". This is the open-curve form. There is no (1/2πi)∮, no winding number and no zeros − poles line. The screenshot shots/rect_sel.png shows the running path leaving the top of the right plane; the plane was not refit.
- Controls on the same F and square: a Disc (c=2, r=0.5) and a 4-vertex Polygon both give the full closed form: "∮γ F(z) dz 6.2832i, (1/2πi)∮ F dz 1, winding −1, zeros − poles 0 − 1 = −1".
- Sector c=1, r=1, t1=-60, t2=60, F=1/(z-1.5), nothing selected: the same "Draw a curve..." text.
- The same sector selected: "Sector 1 ∫γ F(z) dz 1.0986 + 3.1416i". This is worse than the finding says: the value is wrong, not just shown in open form. The pole at 1.5 is inside the sector, so the correct closed-contour value is 2πi. The shown value is ln 3 + πi = 2πi + 2·∫ray2 F dz, because the second ray runs outward (c → c+r·e^{i t2}) when it should run inward. I checked the arithmetic: 2·∫ray2 = 2[log(0.866i) − log(−0.5)] = ln 3 − iπ.
- Phase mode, Cauchy style, F=z^2, rectangle (-1-i, 1+i) selected (its card is expanded): the pane note reads "Cauchy style: select a closed curve or a bounded region in the left plane to see its Cauchy integral here." The plain phase of z^2 is painted everywhere (shots/cauchy_rect.png).

Code cause:
- src/region.js line 18: `seg` always returns `closed:false`; line 24: `arcAng` also returns `closed:false`.
- `K.rect.boundary` (around line 207) returns 4 separate segments. `K.sector.boundary` (around line 256) returns ray(t1), ray(t2) and arc(t1→t2). Both rays point outward, so even joining the pieces in order would not give a closed loop.
- src/app.js `curvePieces` (about line 2107) keeps each piece's `closed` flag, and its orientation step skips pieces that are not closed.
- `integralGeom` (about line 2149) skips the area when nothing is selected: `if (!sel && kindType(s)==='area' && pieces.some(c=>!c.closed)) continue`. Otherwise it sets `closed: comps.every(c=>c.closed)`, which is false for these shapes.
- `cauchyPlot` (about line 2373) needs `x.closed`, so it returns null, and render shows the "select a closed curve" note (about line 1490).
verdict.fix_hint:
Best fix, in src/region.js: give each bounded shape a single closed polygon boundary that goes counterclockwise.
- `K.rect.boundary`: return `[poly([C(x0,y0), C(x1,y0), C(x1,y1), C(x0,y1)].map(...), true)]`, built with `poly(pts, true)`.
- `K.sector.boundary`, when `s.r > 0`: sample one closed polygon c → c+r·e^{i t1} → the arc to t2 (about 96 points) → back to c, as `poly(pts, true)`. If `span === 360` (no rays), return a single `circ`. Keep the current open rays only for the unbounded case `r <= 0`.

This makes `curvePieces`/`integralGeom` mark the shape closed and run the orientation step. That fixes the no-selection skip, the closed-form chip, the Cauchy check at the probe and `cauchyPlot`. It also fixes the wrong sector value, which comes from the second ray being integrated outward (1.0986+3.1416i where 2πi is correct).

Alternative, in src/app.js `curvePieces`: for `t==='area'`, chain the open pieces into one closed loop by matching endpoints, reversing a piece where needed (the sector's ray2 must be reversed), before the orientation step.

Separately, Integral mode should refit the right plane (`fitRight`) when the selection changes which items are integrated. Without that, the 6.2832i endpoint ends up off-screen.

title: Argument principle wrongly says F vanishes or jumps when |F| varies a lot along the curve
repro: Integral mode, one Circle |z|=4, F = e^{z^2}. Also a Circle |z|=17 with F = e^z.
observed: Chip: 'winding of F∘γ about 0 —' and 'F vanishes, blows up or jumps on the curve, so the argument principle does not apply.' Both functions are entire and zero-free. Node check: Calc.argPrinciple(e^{z^2}, |z|=4) returns ok:false.
expected: Winding 0, and the lamp-style agreement 0 − 0 = 0.
fix_hint: calc.js turn(): ctx.tiny = 1e-13 * max|G| over the vertices. Any value below that counts as a zero. Here |e^{z^2}| runs from e^-16 to e^16, so the tiny-but-nonzero values fail. Use a local or absolute test instead: fail only on non-finite values or |g| below about 1e-300, or compare with 1e-13*max(|g0|,|g1|) of the segment being tracked. Let track()'s bisection and linearity check handle real zeros on the curve.

verdict.evidence:
I reproduced the bug in the app and in Node.

In the app: I used the headless harness in test/verify_features_1_cdp with ?ns=verify_features_1, Integral mode, focus 0, and one circle centred at 0 with ci 0. The calc chip (#calcChip) showed:
- e^{z^2}, r=4: "winding of F∘γ about 0 —", then "zeros − poles found inside 0 − 0 = 0", then "F vanishes, blows up or jumps on the curve, so the argument principle does not apply."
- e^z, r=17: the same dash and the same message.
- Controls: e^{z^2} at r=3.5 and e^z at r=10 both show winding 0 and no message.

The lamps at the same time read "●analytic ●entire", so the chip contradicts the entire lamp for a function with no zeros at all. Screenshot: test/verify_features_1_cdp/shots/int_ez2_r4.png. No console errors.

In Node, Calc.argPrinciple on a 128-gon circle returns {winding:0, ok:false, turn:null} for:
- exp(z^2) at r=4 and r=4.2
- exp(z) at r=15 and r=17

exp(z^2) at r=3.5 returns ok:true.

Cause: in src/calc.js turn(), ctx.tiny is set to 1e-13 * max|G| over the vertices. turn() and track() then treat any |g| ≤ ctx.tiny as a zero on the curve. Here min|G|/max|G| is e^-32 ≈ 1.3e-14 (e^{z^2}, r=4) or e^-34 (e^z, r=17), so a nonzero value counts as a zero. For e^z the failure starts at r ≈ 15 (e^-30 ≈ 9.4e-14 < 1e-13). app.js integralExtra() calls Calc.argPrinciple(F, c.flat, 0) with no opts.tiny, so it gets this default.

Fix check: I patched a scratch copy so the default is ctx.tiny = 0.
- t_calc.js still passes 263/263, same as unpatched.
- The reported cases now give ok:true, winding 0.
- e^z·(z−0.5) at r=17 gives 1, e^z/(z−0.5) gives −1, and e^{z^2}(z^3−1) at r=4 gives 3. The original fails all three.
- These stay fail (X), so soundness holds: z−1 on the square (zero at an edge midpoint), z−(1+0.3i) on the square edge, (z−1)^2, 1/(z−1), sqrt z and log z on circles, and z^20−1 with a zero on a vertex.
- Near-curve zeros are still counted correctly: z−1.0000001 gives 0 and z−0.9999999 gives 1.
verdict.fix_hint: In src/calc.js turn(), line 191, stop using a global relative threshold. Change `if (!(ctx.tiny >= 0)) ctx.tiny = 1e-13 * Math.max(...)` to `if (!(ctx.tiny >= 0)) ctx.tiny = 0;`, or use an absolute floor of about 1e-300. Real zeros on the curve are still rejected by the existing exact-zero/non-finite checks and by track()'s depth-44 bisection and linearity test. If a relative guard is still wanted, compare locally inside track() and turn(): |gm| ≤ 1e-13·max(|g0|,|g1|) for the segment being tracked, not against the global max over all vertices. The separate tiny at calc.js:324 (1e-13·typical) has the same relative design. Check whether it causes the same issue for large dynamic ranges before changing it.

title: Contour integrals that are 0 show as rounding noise ('0 + 0i', '0 − 0i', '3.49×10⁻¹⁰ + 1.16×10⁻¹⁰i')
repro: Integral mode, Circle |z|=1, F = z^2 (or z^{-2}, or 1/z over the Annulus 1<|z|<2). Also e^{z^2} on |z|=4.
observed: Chip shows '∮γ F(z) dz 0 + 0i' and '(1/2πi) ∮ F dz 0 − 0i'. For e^{z^2} it shows '3.49×10⁻¹⁰ + 1.16×10⁻¹⁰i' and '1.85×10⁻¹¹ − 5.56×10⁻¹¹i'. This is exactly the Cauchy-theorem case the feature is meant to show, and the noise suggests the theorem fails slightly. The canvas label (CX.fmt) correctly shows 0.
expected: '0' for both rows whenever the value is at the integrator's noise level.
fix_hint: app.js cxShort(w, scale=0) is called without a scale, so tol = 1e-12·max(|re|,|im|) never zeroes a value that is all noise. Return the tolerance scale ∫|F||dz| from Calc.lineIntegral (it is already computed as `scale`), sum it per item, and pass about 1e-9·scale to cxShort for both rows. Also drop any component whose formatted text is '0'.

verdict.evidence:
I reproduced this in my own headless Chrome harness (test/verify_features_2_cdp, ?ns=verify_features_2, command file scratchpad/c1.js). Each run used one shape, one Custom-formula step and rightMode 'integral'. I read the #calcChip .cv texts:
- z^2 on Circle |z|=1: ["0 + 0i", "0 − 0i", "2", "2 − 0 = 2"]. The screenshot (shots/chip_z2.png) shows the chip with "0 + 0i" / "0 − 0i" next to the canvas label "∮ = 0".
- z^{-2} on |z|=1: ["0 − 0i", "0 − 0i", "−2", ...].
- 1/z on Annulus 1<|z|<2: ["0 − 0i", "0 + 0i", "0", ...].
- e^{z^2} on |z|=4: ["3.49×10⁻¹⁰ + 1.16×10⁻¹⁰i", "1.85×10⁻¹¹ − 5.56×10⁻¹¹i", "—", "0 − 0 = 0"].

Cause, from reading the code. In src/app.js:2410, cxShort(w, scale = 0) sets tol = max(1e-12·max(|re|,|im|), 1e-8·scale). The integral rows at app.js:2467 (cxShort(it.value)) and 2471 (cxShort(C(subj.value.im/TAU, -subj.value.re/TAU))) pass no scale. When both components are noise, tol is 1e-12 of the noise itself, so neither component is ever zeroed. Then CX.fmtNum (cx.js:254) prints '0' for |x|<1e-12, but cxShort only checks im===0 numerically. That is how "0 + 0i" / "0 − 0i" appear.

Calc.lineIntegral (calc.js:55-151) computes the ∫|F||dz| `scale` locally but never puts it on `res`, so the app can't currently use it. For e^{z^2} on |z|=4, |F| reaches e^16 ≈ 9e6, so 3.5e-10 is about 1e-17 relative. That is pure noise.

One small correction to the finding: the canvas label (app.js:2357, CX.fmt / numIn with a 1e-12 absolute cutoff) shows 0 only for the tiny-noise cases. For e^{z^2} it would show the 1e-10 noise too.

Side note, not part of this finding: e^{z^2} on |z|=4 also shows winding "—" with "F vanishes, blows up or jumps on the curve", though e^{z^2} has no zeros. The likely cause is arg tracking with very large or small |F|, or the ctx.tiny threshold in calc.js track().
verdict.fix_hint:
1. In src/calc.js lineIntegral, add `res.scale = scale;` before `return res;` (and in the early-return path).
2. In src/app.js integralItems, sum `r.scale` over the components into `it.scale`.
3. In updateCalcChip, call `cxShort(it.value, 1e-1 * it.scale)` (effective tol about 1e-9·∫|F||dz|, since cxShort multiplies by 1e-8) for the ∮ row. For the (1/2πi) row, call `cxShort(C(subj.value.im/TAU, -subj.value.re/TAU), 1e-1 * subj.scale / TAU)`.
4. Make cxShort robust on its own: after formatting, treat a component whose f(x) text is '0' as zero. For example, compute `const rs = f(re), is = f(Math.abs(im));` and then use `if (is === '0') return rs; if (rs === '0') return (im<0?'−':'') + ...`. This way "0 + 0i" / "0 − 0i" can never be printed.
5. Optionally pass the same scale to the canvas label at app.js:2357 so it agrees with the chip.

title: Preimage: the 'Start with a region' card hides the roots and the pulled-back targets
repro: Start with no shapes and add step z^3-1 (or pown n=2 with disc, line and circle targets). Press 6 (Preimage).
observed: The chip lists z₁ = −0.5+0.866i, z₂, z₃ = 1, but the left plane's empty-state card is drawn on top of them. z₁ and z₃ are not visible, and the pulled-back disc |z|<1 and part of the hyperbola are under the card (shots pre_z3m1_left.png, pre_targets.png). This is the main 'find the roots' flow for a new user.
expected: In Preimage the left plane shows the preimages and roots, not an onboarding card.
fix_hint: app.js updateFocusUI: const show = !S.shapes.length && leftStage() === 0 && !S.leftSphere && S.rightMode !== 'preimage'; (or hide the card once targets exist).

verdict.evidence:
I reproduced it with my own harness (test/verify_features_3_cdp, ns=vf3, 1440x900). I loaded a state with no shapes and steps=[custom z^3-1], clicked the right pane and pressed 6.
- State after the key press: rightMode='preimage', left title "z-plane F−1 of the targets", and #calcChip "3 roots of F(z) = 0 in view z₁ −0.5+0.866i, z₂ −0.5−0.866i, z₃ 1".
- #emptyState was still visible (hidden=false). Its card rect is [342,240,300x174] inside paneL [268,44,430x568].
- The left view has 0 at x≈492, y≈335 and 60 px per unit. That puts z₁≈(462,283), z₂≈(462,387) and z₃≈(552,335), all inside the card.
- I took the same clip with and without the card. Shot test/verify_features_3_cdp/shots/pre_zoom_card.png shows only "Start with a region", the formula tags and "Examples". At most a faint ghost of z₂ shows through behind "Examples"; z₁ and z₃ and the dotted unit-circle guide are not visible.
- With the card hidden (pre_zoom_nocard.png), all three ringed root markers z₁, z₂, z₃ and the dotted circle are clearly drawn.
- Full shot: shots/pre_left.png.
Cause in the code: src/app.js updateFocusUI() (about line 2837) uses `const show = !S.shapes.length && leftStage() === 0 && !S.leftSphere;`. This never checks S.rightMode. Default targets (defaultTargets(), a point at 0) always exist, so the Preimage flow with no domain shapes always gets the onboarding card over the roots. CSS .empty-state > div (page.html:479) is an opaque card (92% plane color) with pointer-events:auto, placed at the pane center, which is where the roots and pulled-back targets usually are. The card also blocks pointer input over that area.
The finding is real, and slightly understated: all three roots are covered, not just z₁ and z₃.
verdict.fix_hint: In src/app.js updateFocusUI(), add a mode check: `const show = !S.shapes.length && leftStage() === 0 && !S.leftSphere && S.rightMode !== 'preimage';`. updateFocusUI already runs on every mode switch (app.js ~5569 path), so the card comes back when the user leaves Preimage. Keying on "targets exist" is not enough, because defaultTargets() always supplies a point target. Optionally do the same for 'integral' if its left-plane curves can be drawn without shapes.

title: The left plane's Riemann-sphere view drops all Preimage and Integral content
repro: Preimage mode, F = z^3-1, a disc shape, targets the point 0 and the disc |w|<0.5. Click the globe button in the left header. Then press 7.
observed: The globe shows only the domain disc. No pulled-back target regions, no root markers z₁..z₃, and in Integral no oriented curves, arrows or start dots. The chip still lists the roots. The left title changes from 'F⁻¹ of the targets' to 'on the Riemann sphere'. The tool hint still says 'Drag a shape to move it … Drag empty space to pan', but dragging turns the sphere.
expected: Either show the roots, pullbacks and oriented curves on the globe, or disable the globe in these modes and say so in the hint.
fix_hint: app.js renderLeft returns early to renderSphereLeft (sphereView imageMode only), before drawPullback, drawRoots and drawIntegralCurves. Project the roots and integral curves onto the globe with the leftCam MVP, or disable leftSphereBtn in preimage/integral. In updateFocusUI keep the Preimage role text, and in updateToolHint handle S.leftSphere && rightMode==='preimage'.

verdict.evidence:

Flat view (shots/flat_pre.png): the left plane shows the roots z1, z2, z3 with labels and green rings around them, which are the pullback of |w|<0.5. The title reads 'F−1 of the targets'.

- The globe shows only the checkered domain disc. There are no root markers and no green pullback patches.
- This is not because the roots are on the back. With camL yaw −60° and pitch −24°, z=1 and z=e^{−2πi/3} lie on the equator facing the camera. The '1' label is drawn at that spot with no marker.
- The chip still lists '3 roots of F(z) = 0 in view z₁…z₃'.
- The left title changed to 'on the Riemann sphere'.
- The hint (#toolHint) still reads 'Drag a shape to move it and its handles to reshape. Drag empty space to pan. Targets in the right plane move the same way.'

A drag started on the disc in the left pane (shots/sph_pre_dragged.png) turned the globe: the '−i' label moved. The disc stayed at c=[0,0]. So the hint is wrong.

After pressing 7 for Integral with the globe on (shots/sph_int.png), the globe again shows only the checker, with no oriented curve, arrows or start dot. With the globe off (shots/flat_int.png), the arrowheads and the start dot on the disc's boundary are visible. The right pane and chip still show the closed-curve values.

Code check, src/app.js:
- renderLeft (about lines 1219-1228) returns early to renderSphereLeft when S.leftSphere is set. That skips drawPullback (1234), updateRoots/drawRoots (1238) and drawIntegralCurves (1239).
- sphereView (1690) loops only over S.shapes, never over S.targets, the roots or the integral curves.
- updateFocusUI (2807) sets lrole to 'on the Riemann sphere' before it checks for preimage.
- updateToolHint (3270) uses the sphere-specific text only when S.rightMode !== 'preimage', so preimage falls back to the flat 'drag shape / pan' hint.
- The pointer-down handler (about 4831) always orbits when S.leftSphere is set.

No console errors were logged.
verdict.fix_hint:
src/app.js:
1. In sphereView, or in renderSphereLeft after it returns info, lift each root (from updateRoots) and each sampled integral-curve point to the sphere with lift(). Project them with info.MVP, skipping points where facing() <= 0, as is already done for point shapes. Draw the root dots and labels, and the oriented curve polylines with their arrows and start dot. Pass the pulled-back target areas to GLR.drawSphere as extra regions, or at least draw the target boundaries' preimage. Short of that: disable or grey out #leftSphereBtn when rightMode is 'preimage' or 'integral', and note in the left pane that these overlays need the flat view.
2. In updateFocusUI, when S.rightMode === 'preimage', keep the 'F⁻¹ of the targets' role text and show 'on the Riemann sphere' as a secondary label.
3. In updateToolHint, add a case for S.leftSphere && S.rightMode === 'preimage'. It should say that dragging in the left plane turns the sphere, while targets are still edited in the right plane.

title: Preimage chip omits pole multiplicity, and pole positions when there is more than one
repro: Preimage, target point 0, F = 1/(z-1)^2. Then F = (z^2-1)/(z^2+1), and F = tan z.
observed: For 1/(z-1)^2 the chip reads '0 roots of F(z) = 0 in view, 1 pole 1'. The double pole is shown as '1 pole'; only the canvas label says 'pole ×2'. For (z²−1)/(z²+1) and tan z it reads '2 poles' with no locations, while zeros are listed with values and ×multiplicity. The Calc results are correct (Node: pole×2 at 1; poles at ±i; poles at ±π/2).
expected: Poles listed like zeros, with order and position, e.g. 'pole ×2 at 1', 'poles at i, −i'. Counts should sum the multiplicities.
fix_hint: app.js updateCalcChip (preimage branch): replace the single `${ps.length} pole(s)` row with one row per pole showing ×r.mult and cxShort(r.z), and use ps.reduce(mult) for the count.

verdict.evidence:
I reproduced this in headless Chrome using the harness in test/verify_features_5_cdp, opened with ?ns=verify_features_5. Each run loaded one custom step in Preimage mode with a single point target at [0,0]. These are the #calcChip rows the app showed:
- For \frac{1}{(z-1)^2}: ["0 roots of F(z) = 0 in view", "1 pole1"], which reads "1 pole" with the value 1. In the screenshot (shots/dbl.png) the chip says "1 pole … 1", while the canvas label behind it says "pole ×2". So the solver knows the pole has order 2, but the chip drops it.
- For \frac{z^2-1}{z^2+1}: ["2 roots of F(z) = 0 in view", "z₁−1", "z₂1", "2 poles"]. The poles at ±i are not located.
- For \tan z: ["3 roots …", "z₁−3.1416", "z₂0", "z₃3.1416", "2 poles"]. The poles at ±π/2 are not located.

The code explains it. In src/app.js, updateCalcChip, preimage branch (line 2451):
`${ps.length} pole${ps.length === 1 ? '' : 's'}` … `${ps.length === 1 ? cxShort(ps[0].z, rootScale()) : ''}`
This counts distinct poles, never shows r.mult, and prints a position only when there is exactly one pole. Zeros are counted differently: nz = zs.reduce((a, r) => a + (r.mult || 1), 0) at line 2442, and each zero gets its own row with ×mult (line 2449). The canvas code at line 2086 already writes `pole ×${r.mult}`, and the Integral chip at line 2254 counts poles with multiplicity. So the Preimage chip is the only place that counts and shows poles this way.

The guarantee lamps stayed sound: analytic and rational for the two rational functions, analytic only for tan. No console exceptions appeared apart from one unrelated 404 resource.
verdict.fix_hint:
In src/app.js, updateCalcChip, preimage branch: replace the single summary row at line 2451 with one row per pole, written the same way as the zero rows. For each r in ps, emit `
pole${r.mult > 1 ? ` ×${r.mult}` : ''}${cxShort(r.z, rootScale())}
`. Cap the list like the zeros: use the shared `shown` counter, or a separate cap with an "and N more" line. If you keep a summary count, use np = ps.reduce((a, r) => a + (r.mult || 1), 0) so it matches nz and the Integral chip's zeros − poles count.

title: Double root is listed with numerical noise ("1 − 2.24×10⁻⁷i") depending on viewport
repro: Load the Rational chain (p=1,-1,-1,1; q=1,0,0.25), Disc r=1.6, rightMode preimage, srcView {cx:0,cy:0,s:60}. Read the roots chip at 1440x900, 1100x800 and 390x844 (mobile).

expected: A clean "1" (or a value whose tiny part is below display precision) at every size.
fix_hint: src/app.js:2410-2418 cxShort(): tol = max(1e-12·|parts|, 1e-8·rootScale()) is too tight for a multiple root, whose error is about eps^(1/m). Zero a component when it is below about 1e-6·max(1,|z|) (or below the other component's 4-decimal precision), or scale the tolerance by multiplicity.

verdict.evidence: I reproduced the finding in the headless harness (test/verify_visual_5_cdp, ns=verify_visual_5). Setup: load() with steps=[{type:'rational', params:{p:'1, -1, -1, 1', q:'1, 0, 0.25'}}], a disc of radius 1.6, rightMode 'preimage' and srcView {cx:0, cy:0, s:60}. I read the #calcChip innerHTML at each viewport size. Results: - **1440x900 and 1100x800:** the z₂ ×2 row is `1`. - **390x844 (mobile):** the same row is `1 − 2.24×10⁻⁷i`. The screenshot shots/m390_chip.png shows "z₂×2 1 − 2.24×10⁻⁷i" in the chip. The simple root z₁ = −1 is clean at every size. Cause, confirmed in Node by calling Calc.zerosPoles with the measured left-pane boxes: - Desktop pane is 410x516 px, so the box is ±3.42 × ±4.3. The double root comes out as 1.00000000009 − 3.9e−12i. - Mobile pane is 342x310 px. The same double root comes out as 1.00000035 − 2.243e−7i. So the polish step in calc.js (newton with step hh = 1e−10·(W+H), around lines 367-384 and 471-481) stalls near the multiple root, where the central difference is swamped by rounding. The error it leaves depends on the view box. In cxShort (src/app.js ~2410), tol = max(1e−12·max|part|, 1e−8·rootScale()). rootScale = max(w, h)/s is 342/60 = 5.7 on mobile, so tol is 5.7e−8 and the 2.24e−7 imaginary part survives. On desktop tol is 8.6e−8, and the error is about 4e−12 anyway. The display is also inconsistent: the real part 1.00000035 rounds to "1" at 4 decimals, while noise of the same size in the imaginary part is printed in ×10ⁿ notation.
verdict.fix_hint:
Main fix, in src/app.js cxShort (~line 2410): stop showing a component that is below the display precision of the other one. For example, set im to 0 when |im| < 5e−5·|re| (and the same with re and im swapped), so it is never printed beyond the 4 decimals used for the larger part. Keep the existing absolute tolerance for the case where both parts are tiny.

Another option is to pass r.mult from the roots row (line 2449) into cxShort and widen the tolerance for multiple roots, e.g. tol ≥ 1e−6·rootScale() when mult ≥ 2. A pure eps^(1/m)·scale tolerance (about 1.5e−8·5.7) would still be too tight to hide the 2.24e−7.

A deeper fix belongs in src/calc.js zerosPoles, in the polish loop / newton(). For mult ≥ 2, use a difference step on the order of the current |step| or sqrt(eps)·scale rather than 1e−10·(W+H), or apply Newton to G/G′. The root would then converge to about 1e−8 whatever the view box, so the result would no longer depend on the viewport.

- Light: root dots #831466, pole ⊗ #a0153e.
- Dark: root dots #ea8ec9, pole ⊗ #ff5a85.

These match the tokens exactly.

OKLCH comparison:
- Light: #831466 is L .42, C .165, h 342°. #A0153E is L .46, C .171, h 12°. That is only 30° of hue apart at nearly the same lightness and chroma, ΔE_ok 0.096.
- Dark: #EA8EC9 is h 342°. #FF5A85 is h 8°. ΔE_ok 0.12.

c4 is the palette ink closest to --pole in both themes:
- Light ΔE to pole for c1..c8: .283 .148 .243 .096 .279 .216 .210 .211
- Dark ΔE to pole for c1..c8: .272 .226 .291 .120 .316 .201 .262 .216

- The markers also differ in shape (a filled dot with a ring vs a ring with a cross) and carry labels ("z₁" vs "pole"), so they can still be told apart.
- Spec rule 2 is not literally broken. c4 (#BC4E98, magenta, h 342°) is a shape ink the spec itself defines, and it is not red.

- defaultTargets() (line 222): change ci from 3 to an ink far from --pole. For example, ci 5 (c6 violet, ΔE .216/.201) keeps targets distinct from the first shapes (c1..c3); ci 2 (c3 teal, ΔE .243/.291) also works.

Wrap the draw in GLR.syncCompile = true / false in a try/finally; the gl.js comment already says 'thumbnails (syncDepth) wait as well', but the app never sets it. I reproduced this in my own headless harness (test/verify_regress_0_cdp). Command files were run with q.sh and the screenshots are in test/verify_regress_0_cdp/shots/.

  - Joukowski airfoil: a checkered square, not an airfoil.
  - Quarter plane squared: a plain quadrant.
  - Disk automorphism, Roots as preimages and A residue by integration: almost empty.
  - The data-URL lengths are tiny (798 to 4094 bytes).
  - The console logged repeated "GL_INVALID_VALUE: glGetProgramiv: Program object expected" warnings during that first fill.
- **Same state with GLR.syncCompile = true set before opening (ns=verify_regress_0_sync):** shots/menu_sync.png shows every thumbnail correct, with lengths of 2.7 to 13.5 KB:
  - Strip to disk: a disc with a grid.
  - Joukowski airfoil: an airfoil.
  - Disk automorphism: the morphed disc.
  - Roots as preimages and A residue by integration: their circles and contour.
  - All 11 data URLs differ between the async and sync runs (same = all false).
- **Persistence:** I opened the menu, waited 2 s, pressed Escape, waited 4 s with GLR.compiling = false, then reopened. All 11 img.src values were byte-identical to the wrong first set, and shots/menu_reopen.png still shows the wrong thumbnails. So the exThumbs cache keeps them for the whole session.

Code: src/app.js renderExampleThumb (around lines 5234-5263) swaps in the example's S, calls rebuild() and then setChain, and draws with drawScene. drawScene hard-codes `const sync = false` (around line 749) and passes {cache: false}. In src/gl.js, program() (around lines 1308-1316) finds the new chain's program still pending under KHR_parallel_shader_compile. It then returns the newest ready hist version, which is the user's chain. use()/mapFor feeds that version the example's map spec. The drawScene comment says a thumbnail "is redrawn when the program is ready (renderThumb, GLR.onReady)". That redraw exists only for step thumbnails. The example gallery has no such retry, and exThumbs.set(i, url) caches the wrong image unconditionally.

I did not check the side claim that the menu evicts the user's chain programs (PROG_KEEP=3). After closing the menu, GLR.compiling was false 4 s later.
verdict.fix_hint:
Main fix, in src/app.js renderExampleThumb: make the thumbnail draw wait for its own chain to compile. Put `GLR.syncCompile = true` before the drawScene call and `GLR.syncCompile = false` in a finally block. This is the exact path that produced correct thumbnails in my sync run. The setter changes syncDepth (src/gl.js around line 2718), and getProg then calls finishLink right away whenever syncDepth > 0.

Alternative: after drawScene, check GLR.frameStatus().pending. If it is true, do not store anything in exThumbs; queue the index instead, and redraw it from GLR.onReady (src/app.js around line 5770), the same way step thumbnails use thumbsWaiting.

Optionally, stop the thumbnail draws from evicting the user's chain programs. One way is to restore the user's chain as the current one so evictProgs keeps it. Another is to compile thumbnail programs outside the PROG_KEEP history.

title: Preimage root count drops the solver's 'truncated'/'incomplete' flags, so a capped count reads as exact ('40 roots of F(z) = 0 in view')
repro: State: steps [custom '\frac{z^3-1}{z^2+0.5}', sin], target point p=0, rightMode 'preimage' (F has infinitely many zeros accumulating at ±i/√2). Open the app and read the calc chip.
observed: The chip reads '40 roots of F(z) = 0 in view', lists z₁ = −0.0018 − 0.7122i, z₂ = −0.0018 − 0.7121i and so on, then 'and 34 more'. It never adds the '(first 40)' note, even though Calc.zerosPoles stopped at max=40 and set .truncated.
expected: '40 roots … (first 40)', or 'at least 40'. When the work budget ran out (.incomplete), the count should be marked incomplete rather than shown as exact.
fix_hint: src/app.js updateRoots (around line 2056) pushes { s, sols: sols.filter(...) }. Array.filter returns a new array, which loses the .truncated and .incomplete properties that src/calc.js sets (lines 460, 461, 469), so the chip test at line 2444 (sols.truncated) is never true. Copy the flags onto the filtered array, e.g. const f = sols.filter(...); f.truncated = sols.truncated; f.incomplete = sols.incomplete. Also render .incomplete in the chip.

verdict.evidence:
I reproduced this in my own headless Chrome harness (test/verify_regress_1_cdp, ?ns=verify_regress_1). I loaded steps [custom '\frac{z^3-1}{z^2+0.5}', sin], one point target p=(0,0), rightMode 'preimage', srcView {0,0,60}, and read #calcChip.innerText. It said: "40 roots of F(z) = 0 in view / z₁ 0.0022 − 0.7006i / z₂ 0.0023 − 0.7004i … z₆ 0.0026 − 0.6995i / and 34 more". There was no "(first 40)" note and nothing to show the count was incomplete.

I checked the solver separately in Node with F = sin((z^3-1)/(z^2+0.5)) and target 0, using boxes [-5,5]x[-6,6] and [-6,6]x[-7.5,7.5]. Calc.zerosPoles returned 40 results with truncated=true and incomplete=true. After the same filter that app.js applies, r => r && r.z && CX.isFin(r.z), there were still 40 results, but truncated and incomplete were both undefined.

Cause: src/app.js updateRoots, line 2057, stores `sols: sols.filter(...)`. Array.prototype.filter returns a new array without the expando properties that src/calc.js zerosPoles sets on `out` (lines 426, 434, 436, 460, 461, 469). So the chip check `sols.truncated` (app.js line 2444) can never be true. Nothing in the app reads .incomplete at all. As a result, a count that hit the cap or ran out of work budget is shown as exact.
verdict.fix_hint: In src/app.js updateRoots (line 2057), keep the flags when filtering: `const f = sols.filter((r) => r && r.z && CX.isFin(r.z)); f.truncated = !!sols.truncated; f.incomplete = !!sols.incomplete; out.push({ s, sols: f });`. title: ⌘Z right after scrubbing an integer/angle parameter does nothing
repro: Load the state steps [pown n=3, custom sin z] with a disc. Drag the 'n' label of the Integer power card sideways about 40 px (n goes from 3 to 13). Press ⌘Z (Ctrl+Z also fails), then ⌘Z again.
observed: n stays 13 and nothing is undone; document.activeElement is the number input p1_n. Undo works only after clicking elsewhere: then the same three ⌘Z presses correctly revert the scrub, the move and the handle drag. The toolbar Undo button is still enabled.
expected: ⌘Z right after a scrub undoes the scrub.
fix_hint: src/app.js scrubbable (lines 3794-3818) uses setPointerCapture on the <label for=input>, so the click after the drag always lands on the label. Label activation then focuses the input, and the global keydown handler (line 5927, `mod && key === 'z' && !textEntry`) leaves ⌘Z to the field's empty native undo. Swallow the click that follows a real drag (a one-shot capture-phase click listener calling preventDefault when |dx| > 2 px), or blur the input in up(). The same applies to every angle field (cut θ, φ).

verdict.evidence:
I reproduced this in my own headless Chrome harness (test/verify_regress_3_cdp, ?ns=verify_regress_3, dist/test.html, which is up to date with src: it contains the current scrubbable code). Setup: steps [pown n=3, custom sin(z)] and a disc of radius 1.

Integer field: I dragged the 'n' label (label[for=p1_n], class "pl scrub") 40 px to the right in 10 real CDP mouse moves. p1_n became "13", the saved state became n=13, and the Undo button went from disabled to enabled. The events captured after the drag were, in order: pointerup on LABEL, click on LABEL, focusin on p1_n, click on p1_n. document.activeElement was then p1_n. I pressed Meta+Z and then Ctrl+Z. Both keydowns targeted p1_n with defaultPrevented=false, and p1_n stayed "13" with n=13 in the state. So the app's handler skipped them and the native undo of the number field had nothing to undo. After I called blur() on p1_n, a single Meta+Z restored n to "3".

Angle field: dragging the label of p2_cut (type=number, the cut angle) 40 px to the left changed it from 180 to 170 and focused p2_cut. Meta+Z left it at 170. After blur, Meta+Z restored 180.

Code path: scrubbable() in src/app.js (lines 3794-3818) calls label.setPointerCapture(), so the click synthesized after pointerup is dispatched to the <label for=...>. Label activation then focuses the associated <input type=number>. The pointerdown preventDefault suppresses only the mouse compatibility events, not the click. In the global keydown handler (src/app.js about line 5925-5927), textEntry is true for type=number inputs, so the `mod && key === 'z' && !textEntry` branch is skipped and undo never runs. All three scrubbable call sites (line 3544 and line 3956, which covers both int and angle fields) share this path.
verdict.fix_hint: Fix it in src/app.js scrubbable(). In the pointerdown handler, record the largest |ev.clientX - x0| seen in move(). In up(), if that drag exceeded about 2-3 px, add a one-shot click listener on the label (capture phase, with { once: true, capture: true }) that calls e.preventDefault() and e.stopPropagation(). preventDefault on a label's click cancels its activation, so the input never takes focus. Remove that listener on the next tick (setTimeout 0) in case no click arrives, for example after pointercancel. A simpler alternative is to call input.blur() in up() whenever the scrub moved, but the click still fires after up() and would focus the input again, so suppressing the click is the reliable fix. A plain click with no drag should still focus the input as it does now.

title: Adding a step freezes the display for 170–585 ms per add at mesh 480 (cold chain programs)
repro: Fresh namespace, Mesh quality set to Fine (480). Add 5 steps in turn with '=' + name + Enter (e.g. arcsin, artanh, tanh, Polynomial, Rational). Measure rAF intervals with __qa.frames during each Enter, and run a 10 ms setInterval heartbeat at the same time.
observed: Each add produced one rAF gap: 236, 252, 267, 172 and 265 ms. In another run (cosh, tangent, Cayley, Exponential, Inversion) the gaps were 151, 184, 485, 460 and 586 ms, and the first-ever palette run reached 536 ms. The main thread was mostly free (heartbeat gaps of 45–87 ms), apart from one synchronous getProgramParameter that blocked for 179 ms. Repeating the same chain once its programs were cached gave at most 30–47 ms. Each add compiles 4 chain programs: 8 shaders, about 120 kB of GLSL.
expected: Adding a step does not stall frames by more than a frame or two.
fix_hint: The GPU process stalls the compositor while it compiles the 4 chain programs (region, line and the TF programs), each of which embeds the whole chain source (src/gl.js getProg/startLink, lines 1260-1280). Compile only the program needed for the first paint, and start the others after onReady. Also, do not poll COMPLETION_STATUS synchronously in the same frame as startLink (a sync IPC that waits while the GPU is busy compiling).

verdict.evidence:
I reproduced the stall in my own harness: test/verify_regress_5_cdp, running headless Chrome with ANGLE Metal on an Apple M4, with KHR_parallel_shader_compile present. The command files are in that folder (c2, c3, c4–c8, c12–c17, plus the instrumentation files inst.js, gp.js, cap.js, cap3.js and delay.js). The daemon has been stopped.

1. **Mesh 480 (c3).** Fresh default example, meshN set to 480. Adding cosh, tangent, Cayley (Möbius), Exponential and Inversion with '=' + name + Enter gave one long rAF gap each: 210, 269, 615, 221 and 469 ms. The Exponential add had further gaps of 183 and 135 ms. Each gap starts about 135–150 ms after Enter. The 10 ms heartbeat stayed at or below 17 ms, so the main thread was free. Each add ran 4 linkProgram calls on 117–128 kB of GLSL.
2. **Mesh 240 (c2).** The same behaviour shows at the default mesh, so mesh 480 is not required. The 5 adds gave gaps of 226, 119 (+104), 168, 234 and 193 ms. One add blocked the main thread for 162 ms inside getProgramParameter(0x8B86, ACTIVE_UNIFORMS), which is called from finishLink. This was not the COMPLETION_STATUS poll: every COMPLETION_STATUS query in my logs took 0–0.2 ms.
3. **Cached programs (c3).** Undo, undo, redo, redo of the same chain versions (0 links) gave a worst frame of only 22–31 ms. A chain that Chrome had compiled in an earlier run (the sinh add in c12) also showed no gap.
4. **Map work ruled out (c12).** At mesh 480, editing the Möbius parameter p2_b re-runs all 8 transform-feedback passes with no new programs. The worst frame was 20–25 ms, so the stall does not come from the mesh or transform-feedback work.
5. **The stall comes when the new programs are first used (c16, c17).**
   - With no delay, COMPLETION_STATUS turns true 80–120 ms after Enter, the app uses the programs right away, and the gap follows (189 ms; 244 + 172 + 128 ms).
   - I then made COMPLETION_STATUS report false for 1000–1500 ms, so the programs compiled in the background before the app used them. Three of five adds had no gap over 40 ms (tangent, artanh, arccos).
   - arcsin had a 95 ms gap during the compile. Cayley had a 183 ms gap that moved to just after its first use at 1030 ms.
6. **Same programs, separate context (c8, c13, c14).** I captured the 8 sources of an add, renamed identifiers so nothing was cached, and compiled them in a separate WebGL2 context. Compiling, then 300 ms later running transform feedback and draws with all 4 programs, gave no rAF gap (worst 18.7 ms).

**Conclusion:** the symptom, the numbers and the cached-versus-cold contrast are all real. The cause is narrower than the finding says. The app treats a program as ready, and starts using it in its stage context, when COMPLETION_STATUS first turns true. At that point the GPU process has not finished the compile, so finishLink's synchronous queries and the first draws wait for it, and frames stall.

Two parts of the finding's root cause are wrong:
- The background compile alone mostly does not stall frames.
- The synchronous COMPLETION_STATUS poll is not the blocking call; the ACTIVE_UNIFORMS query in finishLink is.

Also, sources() in src/gl.js puts the whole chain library and chain source in front of the fragment stage too. That includes TF_FS, which only writes zero, and LINE_FS, which does not use the chain. So each add translates and compiles about twice the shader code it needs.

This conflicts with spec section 8.7 ("Add a step: Homotopy starts in ≤ 16ms"): the add-step homotopy (480 ms) freezes for 0.2–0.6 s.
verdict.fix_hint:
All changes are in src/gl.js.

1. **getProg and pollCompiles:** do not call finishLink, which makes the synchronous ACTIVE_UNIFORMS, getActiveUniform and getUniformLocation queries, or draw with a new chain program in the same tick that COMPLETION_STATUS first turns true. Mark the program 'settling' and keep the existing stand-in path (the hist versions, stand()) for one or more polls before switching. The program() and stand() code already supports drawing an earlier chain version.
2. **sources():** put `lib` (GLChain.LIB + ch.info.source + MAP) only in front of stages that use the chain. TF_FS and LINE_FS do not, and REGION_FS should be checked. This roughly halves the GLSL compiled per add.
3. **Stagger the compiles:** compile tfRegion and region first, and start tfLine and line after onReady, so fewer cold programs are in flight when the first draw arrives.

The finding's advice to avoid polling COMPLETION_STATUS synchronously is not the main lever: those polls measured 0–0.2 ms. The blocking call was the getProgramParameter ACTIVE_UNIFORMS query in finishLink.

title: Composite formula TeX grows exponentially with the number of Möbius steps; a 60-step chain throws RangeError and freezes for several seconds
repro: Load a saved chain of 60 steps alternating sin and Möbius (default params) with one disc. Alternatively, with 24 alternating steps, edit a Möbius 'a' to '1.1+i'.
observed: 60 steps: an uncaught 'RangeError: Invalid string length at Object.tex … at fillProps', after which the guarantees panel stops updating, plus a 7.7 s frame stall. 24, 32 and 40 steps: a parameter edit stalls frames for 2.0 s, 3.9 s and over 1.5 s respectively, and the JS heap grows to 109–143 MB.

fix_hint: src/app.js fillProps (around line 4578) composes the full string with `for (const k of act) arg = built[k - 1].tex(arg)` and only then checks arg.s.length >= 700. The Möbius tex substitutes x into both numerator and denominator, so the length doubles per step. Stop composing as soon as the length passes the 700-char limit (keep a budget, or substitute a placeholder symbol), and wrap the call in try/catch.
